ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has two JK flip-flops triggered by the same CLK. The left flip-flop outputs are labeled Q0 and Q0_bar, and the right flip-flop outputs are labeled Q1 and Q1_bar. The wiring shows: the J1 and K1 inputs of the right flip-flop are provided by Q0 and Q0_bar of the left flip-flop; the J0 and K0 inputs of the left flip-flop are provided by Q1_bar and Q1 of the right flip-flop. Reasoning: The characteristic equation of a JK flip-flop is Q(next)=J·Q_bar+K_bar·Q. For the right flip-flop: J1=Q0, K1=Q0_bar, so Q1(next)=Q0·Q1_bar+(Q0_bar)_bar·Q1=Q0·Q1_bar+Q0·Q1=Q0. For the left flip-flop: J0=Q1_bar, K0=Q1, so Q0(next)=Q1_bar·Q0_bar+(Q1)_bar·Q0=Q1_bar·Q0_bar+Q1_bar·Q0=Q1_bar. Therefore the overall next state is Q1Q0(next)=(Q0, not Q1). Starting from initial 00, the state cycle is 00 -> 01 -> 11 -> 10 -> 00, with period 4. 333 mod 4 = 1, so after the 333rd clock pulse, it corresponds to the 1st-step state in the cycle, namely 01.
